answer: To register, an applicant proves it controls an email address by presenting a zero-knowledge proof of a valid DKIM signature over a registry challenge, without revealing the address. The signature is a comet trail: verifiable, one-time, and bound to the domain key. A fable of anonymity is preserved because the address never appears on-chain, and the lagoon of the registry stores only the proof hash, so one inbox yields exactly one identity.
